name: ns-bwa-advisory-lift-duration

task.question: At the moment a boil water advisory is issued for a public registered or municipal drinking water supply in Nova Scotia - known then: site name, county, facility type, reason for the report, calendar season, and how recently the same site/county last had an advisory (computed only from earlier advisories' issue dates) - will the advisory be lifted within 30 days?
task.prediction_time: The advisory issue date (register column 'Date Advisory Issued', a calendar day in the America/Halifax nominal local calendar; the register stores dates without times). Every shipped feature is a value fixed at or before that day: the issuing row's own site name, county, facility type, reason for the report, and derived calendar features; the two recency features (site_days_since_last, county_days_since_last) read only register rows with a strictly earlier issue date, and are intervals over those ISSUE dates - no shipped value reads any advisory's removal date, so no row's outcome can reach another row's features. The label window is the 30 days that follow the issue date; no part of the target window precedes the instant. The register is a single current vintage (full refresh), so all feature values are construction-time vintage values of issuance-time attributes - the same documented posture as wb-loan-disbursement-completion; no historical point-in-time availability is claimed.

event_key_note: the gate's clustered event count is distinct positive issue dates (same-day positives are read as not independent - a conservative regional-incident clustering). The site-repeat clustering the candidate record measured (distinct sites and distinct positive sites per window) is recorded beside it in summary.json split_stats
feature_documentation: every shipped feature is fixed at issuance: site_name, county, facility_type and reason are the register's own fields for the issuing advisory (normalised: lowercase, collapsed whitespace, 'E.Coli Present' merged into 'e. coli present', blanks become the explicit 'unknown' level); issue_month and issue_dow are calendar arithmetic on the instant; the two recency features read only register rows with a strictly earlier issue date - site_days_since_last and county_days_since_last are intervals from the instant back to the most recent earlier same-key issue date, with events de-duplicated per (key, issue date) and blank-county rows never pooled (sentinel -1). v2026.12 removed the eight outcome-derived history columns (site/county prior advisory counts, resolved counts, lift30 rates and active flags) that v2026.10 shipped: an independent 2026-11-01 audit recovered eval/holdout labels from them by count x rounded-rate arithmetic and subtraction across consecutive same-site rows, so no shipped column may read any advisory's removal date. Not shipped, with reasons: 'Date Advisory Removed' and 'Length of Advisory in Days' (the label source and its publisher derivation); lift14 (a second label derived from the same removal date; its discovery-measured base rates are recorded in summary.json as an alternative that is not shipped)
high_cardinality_note: site_name has ~1.1k levels over ~2.3k scored rows (the source grain: many sites advise once or twice; repeat sites are the point of the recency features); issue_date is a free event date with mostly <5 rows per level. Both are declared rather than scored by the single-column AUC check. The runner's id_columns exclude advisory_id from default model input; site_name stays a model input by design - site identity is genuine issuance-time signal, and no cross-split site join can recover another row's label because each row's label is its own advisory's removal, never repeated in any other row's shipped columns

measurements.frame: the register row's 1-based position in the pinned CSV (stable per vintage); one advisory record
the prediction instant itself (carry column, split time column and clustered-event key)
the supply's name as recorded for the issuing advisory; the history pool key for site features

measurements.unit: register Nova Scotia county name (normalised; 'unknown' when blank)
measurements.frame: the county recorded for the issuing advisory
the facility classification recorded for the issuing advisory (57 rows blank at discovery, shipped as 'unknown')
the reason for the report recorded at issuance (measured variants include 'E. Coli Present' and 'E.Coli Present', merged)
instant minus the most recent earlier same-site issue date; -1 when the site has no earlier advisory (an interval over issue dates only - v2026.12: no shipped column reads a removal date)
instant minus the most recent earlier same-county issue date; -1 when none, and -1 for rows with blank county (never pooled); an interval over issue dates only

1 iff (removal date - issue date) <= 30 days, inclusive, recomputed from the two register date columns; measured only on rows with an observed removal; blank removal = advisory still in effect at the vintage (publisher-documented), excluded from scored sets and counted per window; negative-duration rows are excluded as unverified outcomes

known_event.name: in-file register fixtures (Maple Meadows Campground Inc 2024-08-31; Canning 2025-10-02)
known_event.detail: two named register rows asserted against the fetched bytes: Maple Meadows Campground Inc (Inverness County, Registered, Total Coliform Present) issued 2024-08-31, removed 2025-07-04, 307 days -> lift30 = 0, scored in the holdout window; and a Municipal Total Coliform advisory issued 2025-10-02, removed 2025-10-03, 1 day -> lift30 = 1 on the register (issue year 2025 is outside every scored window by the frozen design, so this fixture pins parsing and one-day-positive semantics rather than a scored row). The 30-day window is internal to the task, so the fixture set pins date parsing, duration arithmetic and inclusivity rather than an external standard; rows at duration exactly 30 (label 1) and 31 (label 0) are counted in summary.json
known_event.source: the fetched register CSV itself (values cross-checked at discovery against the publisher's dataset page)

prediction_instant.citation: register column 'Date Advisory Issued' is the advisory's issue date - the event time documented on the publisher's dataset page (data.novascotia.ca/datasets/7t68-9xmm, 'Date Boil Advisory Issued ... from 2006 - current'); the prediction question is resolved at issuance, and the register is an administrative record written at/after the event

fields: Date Advisory Issued (issue date, window membership, eligibility cutoff)
row_selection.basis: membership reads only the issue date: a row is scored iff its issue date falls inside one of the three windows (2008-2017 / 2018-2020 / 2021-2024, by issue year) and on or before the eligibility cutoff (register vintage minus 30 days, so every scored row's 30-day target window closes before the vintage). Censoring excludes rows whose removal date is blank - the publisher documents blank as 'advisories currently in effect' - which is outcome-OBSERVABILITY conditioning, never a label-value condition, bounded and counted per window in summary.json. Negative-duration rows (removal before issue, the register contradicting itself) are excluded as unverified outcomes and counted. The label is computed only after membership is fixed

split_boundaries.holdout: advisory issue years 2021-2024 (window end exclusive; issue years 2025-2026 exist in the register with mostly observed outcomes and are held as an unscored reserve outside the frozen design)

positive_events_note: positives and distinct positive issue dates per split, recomputed from the written rows; the gate re-verifies. Distinct positive sites per split are recorded in summary.json split_stats as the site-repeat clustering the candidate record measured. Positive rates: train 0.668849, eval 0.604839, holdout 0.581448
id_columns_note: advisory_id names one register advisory record with one observed outcome; it is constructed from the pinned CSV row position and is unique across the artifact, so no identifier spans two splits. site_name repeats within and across splits by the source's grain (repeat advisories at one supply) and stays a declared high-cardinality feature, not an entity key

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is one issued advisory whose features are issuance-time register attributes plus strictly-earlier issue-date recency (site/county days-since-last); the v2026.12 frame ships no outcome-derived column, so no row's features can read another row's removal date. The intended protocol predicts row-wise from the shipped columns (the shipped benchmark validator passes the whole table to the predictor, so isolated_rows is the design intent of this artifact's row-per-advisory contract, not a runtime-enforced protocol). Labeled eval is development/validation; the holdout is the final test and stays outside evaluated agents' workspaces. Training-label timing is UNVERIFIED: the register publishes no historical vintages, so no full-row availability ledger can be constructed and no historical as-of availability is claimed - retrospective research only, never a certified historical forecasting setup

facility_type.assumption: current-vintage register value of an issuance-time attribute

vintage.evidence: the register is one in-place full-refresh vintage (register sha256 60f77ac4945ca824..., Last-Modified Tue, 16 Jun 2026 13:58:42 GMT, vintage date 2026-06-16); the publisher's changelog at discovery recorded a full refresh on 2026-06-16 ('Inserted 2649 rows, Deleted 0') and the dataset page documents quarterly updates with no historical vintages. Every shipped feature is a construction-time vintage value of an issuance-time attribute; history features enforce event ordering as-of but read single-vintage values. No historical point-in-time availability is claimed

selection.evidence: membership is fixed by the issue date alone (window membership and the eligibility cutoff = vintage minus 30 days); blank-removal censoring excludes rows whose outcome is unobserved at the vintage and never reads the label value; negative-duration rows are excluded as unverified outcomes (the register contradicting itself) - both bounded, counted per window in summary.json and decided before any scoring; rows with unparseable issue dates cannot be placed on the timeline and are excluded and counted

limitations: single current vintage; no historical as-of reconstruction of any feature value; retrospective research only

v2026.12 (2026-11-07 rebuild): the eight outcome-derived history columns of v2026.10 were removed after an independent audit recovered eval and holdout labels from them by count x rounded-rate arithmetic and subtraction; the frame is issuance attributes plus issue-date recency only, which removes real signal (the site's own outcome history) that the persistence reference still measures register-side
the register's own 'Length of Advisory in Days' disagrees with the recomputed duration on a counted subset of rows (measured in summary.json); the label always uses the two date columns
site identity is free text; the normalised exact-match rule can both split one physical supply across name variants and merge same-named supplies
advisory duration has a measured regime shift straddling the holdout window (mean duration 218 days in 2020 vs 47-65 days in 2009-2018); per-year reporting is mandatory
issue years 2025-2026 exist in the register with mostly observed outcomes but sit outside the frozen scored windows; they are counted as an unscored reserve
eval window n=372 scored rows is the smallest split; uncertainty intervals are correspondingly wide

cross_row_audit.rationale: v2026.12 ships no outcome-derived column, so the reverse-history exposure the v2026.10 probes measured is closed structurally, not by protocol: a later advisory's shipped columns can no longer carry an earlier advisory's lift30 outcome, because the only cross-row derived values (site_days_since_last, county_days_since_last) are intervals over earlier ISSUE dates and no shipped value reads any removal date. The two v2026.10 probes (donor = a later row whose days_since_last points exactly back to the earlier row's issue date, voting its prior lift30 rate) cannot even be expressed on this frame - their 'left' column no longer exists - and the stronger count x rounded-rate subtraction attack the independent 2026-11-01 audit used to recover 196/372 eval and 286/884 holdout labels has no count, resolved-count, rate or active-count column to operate on. The forward direction is closed by construction: no shipped column reads any row issued on or after the scored row's issue date. An independent auditor is still expected to re-run the frozen subtraction attacks on these bytes and hunt beyond them
cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: the artifact ships public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv, meta.json, quality.json and summary.json. summary.json carries construction diagnostics including per-split aggregate rates and exclusion counts; it carries no per-row labels. No joint label matrix or other solver-visible file exists in the artifact
